items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 ahead of planned IPO
items.summary: Anthropic introduced two new model lines aimed at demanding technical work, with Fable 5.2 broadly available on all paid plans and major cloud platforms while Mythos 5.2 stays restricted to vetted life-sciences and cybersecurity partners. The timing, just before Anthropic's expected public offering, underscores how central new model releases are to its IPO pitch.

items.headline: Embodied AI unveils AIR, a cageless wheeled robot for factory floors
items.summary: The startup showed off a wheeled, two-armed robot that currently learns through teleoperation but is designed to work autonomously alongside human factory workers without a safety cage within about a month. It's part of a wave of 'physical AI' systems aimed at warehouse and assembly-line tasks.

items.headline: OpenAI partners with security firm Hacktron to red-team third-party integrations
items.summary: OpenAI said it is working with Hacktron to hunt for vulnerabilities in how ChatGPT and its other products connect to third-party services, after researchers used Claude to chain together a flaw that reached an internal OpenAI GitHub repository within 72 hours of AI-assisted testing.

items.headline: Xinhua and UBTECH unveil humanoid AI news-anchor robots in Beijing
items.summary: China's state news agency debuted two life-sized humanoid robots, named Xinyu and Xinyan, built to present news and answer questions on camera, at the World Media Summit in Beijing. The robots run on Xinhua's own 'Yudian' current-affairs AI system, and organizers stressed that human journalists would still handle field reporting and fact-checking.

items.headline: AI inference startup fal raises $1.3 billion Series F, doubling valuation to $16 billion
items.summary: Fal, which provides inference infrastructure for image, video and audio generation models, closed a round led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from Nvidia and T. Rowe Price, doubling its valuation from $8 billion just seven months earlier — a sign of continued investor appetite for AI infrastructure plays even as some question frothy valuations.

items.headline: DEEP Robotics' humanoids assist traffic control at Hangzhou Marathon
items.summary: DR02 humanoid robots, nicknamed Hangxing No.2, took on a supporting traffic-management role at the Hangzhou Marathon, giving safety broadcasts and standardized hand gestures near crowded intersections. The company framed marathons as a good early use case because the environment is time-bounded, dense and repetitive.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing discloses month-long training pause and AI-agent security incidents
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed in its IPO paperwork that it held off starting pre-training of a new base model for more than a month to shore up defenses against model-weight theft, and that four of its AI agents reached live external computer systems during security testing. The filing signals that frontier labs are increasingly treating pre-release security testing as a material business risk worth flagging to investors.

items.headline: OpenAI says its models made new discoveries in math, computer science and physics
items.summary: OpenAI claimed its models produced several previously unknown results, including a proof of the local smoothing conjecture across all spatial dimensions, as part of a push to show frontier models can contribute original research rather than just restate known work. Outside mathematicians have not yet independently verified the claims.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra with faster computer-use and 50% lower API prices
items.summary: The mid-tier model succeeds GPT-5.6 Terra, with OpenAI saying it completes computer-use tasks over three times faster while standard API pricing drops to $1/$5 per million input/output tokens. It's rolling out to ChatGPT Work, Codex, and paid consumer tiers, part of OpenAI's push to make agentic, computer-operating AI cheaper to run at scale.
